fields.resell_eur: [min, max] typical resale price, good condition
fields.buy_eur: [min, max] purchase price that leaves margin
fields.in_production: true if the model (or an official reissue) is still sold new
fields.official_url: brand-level official site, null if brand is defunct or URL unknown

meta.caveat: Prices are estimates from general market knowledge, not checked against sold listings. URLs point to brand sites, not product pages.

items.description: 1958 Poul Henningsen pendant. Older versions and rare colours sell best. Check for dents and original shades.
72-leaf pendant from 1958. Copper and steel versions most wanted. Count the leaves and check each for dents.
Glass three-shade table lamp. Pre-war originals reach 5K+. Chipped glass shades kill the value.
Eight-shade white pendant. Large and fragile, so local pickup deals are often cheap.
Arne Jacobsen 1957 floor lamp for the SAS hotel. Early versions with metal base details sell higher.
Verner Panton 1971 mushroom floor lamp. Acrylic shade scratches and yellowing are the main issues.
Castiglioni 1962 arc lamp with Carrara marble base. Many copies. Check Flos stamp and marble chips.
Castiglioni table lamp with glass bowl diffuser. Older glass versions beat the newer plastic small one.
1967 marble base table lamp. Black and green shades most common. Check marble and glass disc.
Vico Magistretti 1977 table lamp. Large 233 size in metal or opal glass is the one buyers search for.
Gae Aulenti 1965 telescopic lamp. Check that the height mechanism holds and the shade has no cracks.
1969 acrylic sphere pendant with inner reflectors. Vintage Louis Poulsen versions sell above Verpan reissues.
1970s bamboo and rice paper fan lamps. Fragile, condition is everything. Prices rose sharply since 2020.
1960s Dutch glass block wall and ceiling lamps. Often listed without the brand name, which is where deals are.
J. Hoogervorst 1950s Dutch wall and floor lamps with counterweight. Brass details and original shade matter.
1930s Dutch modernist Giso series. Look for the Giso stamp and intact opaline glass.
French industrial articulated lamp from 1950. Old workshop originals with patina sell above new ones.
Christian Dell 1930s Bauhaus desk lamp. Pre-war originals have embossed 'Original Kaiser-Idell' on the shade.
Washi paper light sculptures. Check for the sun and moon stamp. Torn paper is hard to repair.
1950s originals are auction pieces. Most listings are copies. Only buy with provenance or a numbered reissue.
Star-shaped Columbus Gilco tubes. Art Decor paint and Campagnolo groups drive the price.
1984 anniversary frame with ornate lugs. Rare. Chrome condition and original fork are key.
1990s carbon lugged frame, Mapei team bike. Mapei livery sells highest. Inspect lugs for cracks.
1970s-80s steel classics. Clover cutouts in lugs. Saronni red and Molteni orange are favourites.
1980s Columbus SLX frame with heart cutouts. Strong collector base in Italy, Japan and Benelux.
1980s top steel model. Spumoni and chrome finishes sell best. Check chrome for pitting.
Vintage celeste steel race bike. Original paint and decals are worth more than a respray.
Columbus SLX frame from the late 1980s. 7-Eleven, Motorola and Telekom team paint adds 30-50%.
1990s Columbus MAX oversized steel. Motorola team livery is the grail version.
Lugged steel frame made since the 1950s. Older ones with the winged C logo carry a premium.
1980s TIG-welded aero frame with fins. Very rare, around 300 made. Verify with serial and Cinelli archive.
Handbuilt in Grosseto. Chrome lugs and detailed paint. Less known, so pricing is softer than Colnago.
Gios blue Brooklyn team bike from the 1970s. Coin inlays in the fork crown identify originals.
TI-Raleigh team frame in Reynolds 753, built in Ilkeston. SB serial number confirms the workshop.
Dutch Reynolds 531 race frame from 1970s-80s. Plenty on Marktplaats. AA-Special is the top version.
Japanese-built top model for the Dutch market. Dura-Ace equipped versions sell fastest.
Frames from the Westerstraat workshop in Amsterdam. Local cult status, mostly sold within the Netherlands.
French Reynolds 531 racer with Nervex lugs. White with rainbow stripes. French parts are hard to replace.
First carbon frame to win the Tour, 1986. La Vie Claire Mondrian paint is the one to find.
Pre-Trek aluminium frames with fade paint jobs. Chehalis-built before 2002. Check for dents and cracks.
1956 lounge chair with ottoman. Rosewood pre-1990 is top tier. Check shock mounts and veneer cracks.
Aluminium Group office chairs. Office liquidations sell them in batches far under single-unit price.
Padded leather version of the Aluminium Group. Leather condition and gas lift function set the price.
Arne Jacobsen 1958. Leather sells for double fabric. Label under the seat and star base confirm it.
Arne Jacobsen 1958. Reupholstery costs 600+, so price worn fabric examples accordingly.
Poul Kjaerholm 1956. E. Kold Christensen production is worth 2-3x Fritz Hansen. Check the frame stamp.
Wegner 1949 dining chair. Sells in sets of 4-6. Paper cord seat replacement costs about 150.
Wegner 1950 lounge chair with woven paper cord seat and back. Cord condition is the whole story.
Wegner plank armchair in oak or teak. Often sold with tired cushions, which are cheap to redo.
Wegner 1951 wing chair. Original AP Stolen production is the collector version.
Borge Mogensen 1958 oak and saddle leather. Patina on leather is a plus, tears are not.
Mies van der Rohe 1929. Heavily copied. Knoll signature stamped in frame on newer ones.
Marcel Breuer 1925 tubular steel. Gavina and early Knoll versions are the ones worth buying.
Eero Saarinen 1948. With ottoman is worth about 30% more. Foam in old ones often needs replacing.
Le Corbusier 1928 cube armchair. Frame is engraved with signature and serial number.
Le Corbusier and Perriand 1928. Pony hide version most wanted. Serial number on the frame.
Pierre Paulin 1960. Dutch-made, so supply on Marktplaats is good. Reupholstered in boucle sells fast.
Pierre Paulin 1966. Sculptural single-piece seat on a lacquered wood base. Check base for chips.
Pierre Paulin 1960. Two identical shells on a chrome frame. Pairs sell better than singles.
Martin Visser 1960s easy chairs. Saddle leather SZ02 is the top one. Wicker versions need intact weave.
W.H. Gispen 1934 tubular lounge chair. Pre-war originals sell well above reissues.
Michel Ducaroy 1973. Price is per element. Full sets of 5 reach 8-12K. Check for the label underneath.
1972 modular 'Non Stop' sofa. Price depends on element count, around 500-900 per piece.
Mario Bellini 1970 modular sofa. Vintage sets in original fabric outsell the 2020 reissue.
Chrome and saddle leather chairs from the Les Arcs ski resort. Often sold in sets from French sellers.
1950s teak and cane from Chandigarh. Flooded with replicas. Needs provenance and painted inventory marks.
1970s Brazilian leather and jacaranda lounge chair. Lafer label under the seat. Leather straps wear out.
Alvar Aalto 1936 with wide birch cantilever arms. Zebra fabric is the signature version.
The original motorcycle jacket. 613 has stars on the epaulettes. Older label versions sell higher.
British biker jackets since the 1950s. Aviakit label. Big demand from Japan.
Heavy competition-weight leather made in Massachusetts. Sizing runs small, list measurements.
Scottish-made horsehide jacket. Niche but loyal buyers on forums and in Japan.
1980s-90s leather varsity and flight jackets. Big patches and embroidery raise the price.
1990s all-over team leather jackets. Bulls and Lakers lead. Many fakes, check stitching and labels.
Slim asymmetric lamb leather biker. Black sells fastest. Sizes 46-50 move quickest.
Oversized shearling aviator. Seasonal: buy in spring and summer, sell from October.
Pre-1953 single pocket denim jacket with cinch back. Big E tab. Repros exist, check rivets and tab.
1953-1962 two-pocket pleated denim jacket. Large sizes are rare and worth much more.
1960s trucker with capital E on the red tab. Small e versions are worth under 100.
Blanket-lined denim jacket with corduroy collar. 1950s-60s labels are the valuable ones.
Late 1980s thermo-sensitive fabric that changes colour. Check that the effect still works.
1982 first-collection jackets in military tarp fabric. Green-edge badge. Archive collectors pay up.
1988 Massimo Osti design with goggles in the hood. Pre-2000 pieces are the collectable ones.
Gore-Tex Pro shell. Made in Canada versions carry a premium. Check seam tape for delamination.
1990s Scot Schmidt ski jacket. Bold colour blocking. Originals outsell the reissues.
Seasonal Supreme collaborations since 2007. Specific prints vary a lot. Fakes are common.
1980s shiny down jackets. Check cartoon label and logo stitching to rule out fakes.
The original Antarctic parka. Hologram label inside confirms it. Seasonal demand peaks in November.
Blanket-lined duck canvas work jacket. Faded 1990s USA-made pieces sell for more than new ones.
Japanese reproduction of the WWII flight jacket in horsehide. Retail is 2K+, so used holds value.
Waxed cotton motorcycle jacket since 1948. Made in England pre-2000 pieces are the target.
1980s-90s colour-blocked racing jackets. Bought as fashion now, so bold colours win.
Boucle jacket with chain-weighted hem. Lagerfeld-era 1990s pieces are most wanted. Check buttons.
1999-2004 archive pieces with interior straps. Label font and made in Italy tag date them.
Made in England gabardine trench. 'Burberrys' label means pre-1999. Complete belt and D-rings matter.
5.5m Frisian polyester sloep. Price depends heavily on engine: inboard diesel hours and year.
Popular Dutch family sloep. Holds value well. Check for osmosis and engine service records.
Classic-look sloep with teak details. Teak deck condition decides whether it is a deal.
Compact tender-style sloep, popular for Amsterdam canals. Sells fast between April and June.
Tender sloep with outboard or inboard. Outboard versions are easier to resell.
Higher-end sloep from Friesland. Older examples fall into this budget. Strong demand in spring.
6.5m Van de Stadt open keelboat. Active Dutch class association keeps prices stable.
1917 Dutch national one-design class. Wooden hulls need upkeep. Class registration number matters.
1933 Dutch wooden one-design keelboat. Racing pedigree and sail inventory move the price.
The standard Dutch sailing school boat. Ex-rental fleets sell cheap in autumn.
Swedish GRP folkboat by Tord Sunden. Seaworthy and loved. Check deck core and rigging age.
1942 clinker design. Wood hulls are cheaper but costly to maintain. GRP versions resell easier.
Swedish cruiser, over 3,400 built. Circumnavigation reputation. Engine replacement is the main cost.
British long-keel cruiser with ocean-crossing history. Small cabin, strong following.
Dutch-built cruiser known for solid construction. Well regarded in the local market.
1970s Swedish bluewater cruiser. Brand name carries the price. Teak deck state is the big risk.
British open day sailer with tan sails. Trailer included adds 1-2K. Loyal owner community.
Gaff-rigged trailer sailer since 1979. Holds value better than almost any small cruiser.
One-design racer with an active Dutch fleet. Sail age and trailer decide the deal.
Most popular one-design keelboat built. Check for wet deck core and keel sump repairs.
Foam-filled unsinkable hulls. Classic 1970s-80s with mahogany interior are collected. Check for water in foam.
C.G. Pettersson Swedish salon boats from 1910-1950. Each is unique. Budget for a hull survey.
1960s-70s Danish sport cruisers with a retro following. Old Volvo petrol engines are the weak spot.
Swedish 1970s displacement cruiser with aft cabin. Frugal diesel. Popular on Dutch inland water.
Norwegian double-ender cruiser. Solid reputation. AK and AC versions differ in cabin layout.
Dutch steel cruisers from the 1970s. Hull thickness measurement report is a must before buying.
Resells above retail. Togo and Epsom leather in neutral colours move fastest. Authentication required.
Sellier (stiff) beats Retourne. Vintage box leather Kellys from the 1960s-90s are the entry point.
H-clasp shoulder bag from 1959. Vintage 23cm in box leather is the most accessible.
Crossbody with perforated H. PM size in Clemence leather has the widest buyer pool.
Bucket bag. Size 18 is the most wanted. Lock and key must be included.
Tote in leather or canvas. Full leather Negonda sells about 40% above canvas.
Caviar leather holds up better than lambskin. Serial sticker and card must match.
Mademoiselle lock and all-chain strap. Aged calfskin hides wear well.
1989-1995 single flap named after Princess Diana. Discontinued, 24k gold-plated hardware.
Entry-level Chanel. Black caviar with gold hardware sells within days.
Monogram canvas classic. Honey patina on handles is fine, cracks in canvas are not. Check date code.
Weekend duffle. Bandouliere version with strap sells about 200 higher.
Most liquid LV bag. Including the pouch adds 150-250. Check corners and strap glazing.
Structured dome bag. Epi leather and Vernis versions sell alongside Monogram. BB size is trending.
Small shoulder pouch. Price doubled since 2019. Cheap to ship, easy to flip.
2003 Takashi Murakami collab in 33 colours. White more wanted than black. Y2K demand is high.
John Galliano 1999 design. Vintage Oblique canvas and rare prints lead. Relaunched in 2018.
Cannage quilted top handle from 1995. Medium in black lambskin is the reference. All charms must be there.
1997 shoulder bag. Sequin, beaded and embroidered editions sell far above Zucca canvas.
2009 top handle with twist lock. Regular size in Selleria leather keeps value best.
1960s hobo with piston clasp. Vintage GG canvas pieces are plentiful and still rising.
1947 design with heat-bent bamboo handle. Check the bamboo for cracks, they cannot be fixed.
Reissue of the 2005 nylon shoulder bag. Original 2000s nylon pieces sell for 300-600.
Knotted intrecciato hobo from the Daniel Lee era. Mini and Teen sizes sell fastest.
Wide-weave crossbody. Padded version in seasonal colours is discounted more than black.
Phoebe Philo 2010 design. Micro and Nano sizes. Old logo with accent on the E marks Philo era.
Box calfskin flap bag. Scratches show easily, so clean examples are rare and priced up.
2001 Nicolas Ghesquiere design. Early chevre leather pieces from 2003-2007 are the collector ones.
Jonathan Anderson 2015 geometric bag. Small size in tan or black is the liquid configuration.
Hand-painted chevron tote. No online sales by Goyard, which keeps resale close to retail.
Belgian house, 1958 design with D buckle. Underpriced in NL and BE listings versus Paris resale.
Tom Ford 2002 hobo with horn handle. Y2K revival piece. Check horn for chips.
2005 it-bag with oversized padlock. Relaunched in 2025, which lifted prices on originals.
